Write a key as a spreadsheet

Source: R/spreadsheet.R
keyToSpreadsheet.Rd

Writes a key as the CSV file that keyFromSpreadsheet() reads, so that a key imported from FishBase or generated from data can be opened in Excel or Google Sheets, edited by hand and read back. The columns are those of the Montana template: Couplet, Choice, Question, Description, Goes to, Species and Photo, followed by Note and Label when the key's leads have them (a pruned key has notes, see pruneKey(); a PhyloTree key has labels).

Usage

keyToSpreadsheet(key, file, photos = NULL, bom = TRUE)

Arguments

key

A dimoose key.

file

Path of the CSV file to write (UTF-8).

photos

Folder to write the key's embedded photos into; by default the folder the CSV file is in. It is created if needed.

bom

Start the file with a byte-order mark? Excel needs one to show accented and other non-English letters correctly when the file is opened by double-clicking; Google Sheets and keyFromSpreadsheet() read the file either way. Use FALSE for programs that do not expect one.

Value

file, invisibly, so the result can go straight to keyFromSpreadsheet().

Details

Photos embedded in the key (see imageMeta()) are written as image files into photos, named by their ids, and the Photo column names those files. A file of that name that is already there with different contents is left alone and used as it is, so writing a key back next to its original photos does not replace them with the smaller embedded copies. Pictures a lead refers to by web address stay web addresses.

Reading the file back gives the same leads and the same photo ids. The exceptions are small: a photo id that cannot be a file name (it has a /, :, comma or the like in it, or differs from another only by capitals) is changed, with a message; a line break inside a cell comes back as a plain line feed whatever it was; and leads without a Choice are lettered.

A spreadsheet holds only those columns. Anything else in the key's leads (for example the taxon links of a FishBase key, or the tests of a key a machine can follow) is not written, and a message says which columns were left out; the title and citation are not written either, so pass desc and meta again to keyFromSpreadsheet().

See also

keyFromSpreadsheet()

Examples

dir <- tempfile("key")
dir.create(dir)
csv <- keyToSpreadsheet(montanaKey(), file.path(dir, "montana.csv"))
list.files(dir)
#>  [1] "acer_glabrum_leaf.jpg"           "acer_negundo_leaf.jpg"          
#>  [3] "betula_occidentalis_bark.jpg"    "betula_papyrifera_bark.jpg"     
#>  [5] "betula_papyrifera_leaf.jpg"      "feature_flat_petiole.jpg"       
#>  [7] "fraxinus_pennsylvanica_leaf.jpg" "montana.csv"                    
#>  [9] "populus_angustifolia_leaf.jpg"   "populus_deltoides_leaf.jpg"     
#> [11] "populus_tremuloides_bark.jpg"    "populus_trichocarpa_leaf.jpg"   
#> [13] "quercus_macrocarpa_acorn.jpg"    "quercus_macrocarpa_leaf.jpg"    
#> [15] "salix_amygdaloides_leaf.jpg"    
# ... edit the file in a spreadsheet program, then read it back
again <- keyFromSpreadsheet(csv, desc = "Montana trees, edited")
identical(again$leads$Character, montanaKey()$leads$Character)
#> [1] TRUE
